title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Ten named destinations along downtown Milledgeville corridors, each paired with one specific reason to step beyond campus.

cards.title: See a Flexible Stage
cards.subtitle: West Hancock Street corridor
cards.notes: Walk east along West Hancock Street to check the theatre schedule and see how the flexible seating changes with each production.
cards.short_summary: A downtown performance space configured for varied staging styles.
cards.evidence_claim: The Campus Black Box Theatre is at 137 West Hancock Street and has flexible seating designed for multiple staging configurations.
cards.access_notes: Performance access depends on the current theatre schedule and ticketing; check before visiting.

cards.title: Start with the Walking-Tour Map
cards.subtitle: West Hancock Street corridor
cards.notes: Begin at 200 West Hancock Street and pick up the self-guided historic-walking-tour brochure before choosing a downtown route.
cards.short_summary: A practical launch point for exploring the historic district on foot.
cards.evidence_claim: The Visitor Information Center is located at 200 West Hancock Street, and the local tourism bureau directs visitors there for the historic walking-tour brochure.
cards.source_title: Things to Do in Milledgeville, GA | 2-day Itinerary
cards.access_notes: Visit during information-center operating hours to obtain a brochure; confirm current hours before setting out.

cards.entity_name: The Floyd L. Griffin, Jr. Black Heritage Plaza
cards.title: Read the Black Business District Marker
cards.subtitle: North Wayne Street corridor
cards.notes: Head to North Wayne Street and pause at the permanent monument documenting the commercial district once known as the Strip.
cards.short_summary: A public-history stop preserving the story of Milledgeville’s Black business district.
cards.evidence_claim: The plaza at 201 North Wayne Street contains a permanent monument commemorating the city’s Black history and the former African American business district.
cards.source_title: The Floyd L. Griffin, Jr. Black Heritage Plaza
cards.access_notes: The listing describes an outdoor plaza with tables and chairs; event access may vary when performances are scheduled.

cards.title: Catch a Rotating Gallery Exhibit
cards.subtitle: North Wayne Street corridor
cards.notes: Continue along North Wayne Street and check the current Marlor Art Gallery exhibition before entering the historic arts center.
cards.short_summary: Changing exhibitions give this Wayne Street arts stop a fresh focus.
cards.evidence_claim: The John Marlor Art Center at 201 North Wayne Street houses the Marlor Art Gallery, whose visiting-artist exhibitions change bimonthly.
cards.access_notes: Check Allied Arts exhibition dates and gallery access before visiting; programs and workshops may require registration.

cards.title: Plan an Oconee River Outing
cards.subtitle: North Wayne Street corridor
cards.notes: Stop at 112 North Wayne Street to ask about current rentals, river shuttles, and the equipment needed for a future outing.
cards.short_summary: A downtown planning stop for paddling or cycling beyond the block.
cards.evidence_claim: Oconee Outfitters at 112 North Wayne Street offers kayak, canoe, paddleboard and bicycle rentals plus shuttle service to the Oconee River.
cards.access_notes: The listing gives Monday hours of noon–6 p.m. and Tuesday–Saturday hours of 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; confirm before visiting.

cards.title: Browse New and Vintage Vinyl
cards.subtitle: North Wayne Street corridor
cards.notes: Walk to 124 North Wayne Street and browse the genre-spanning record bins during the shop’s posted Wednesday–Saturday window.
cards.short_summary: A compact downtown record stop with both new and vintage titles.
cards.evidence_claim: Wax Galaxy Records at 124 North Wayne Street carries hundreds of new and vintage vinyl titles across multiple genres.
cards.access_notes: The current listing states Wednesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; confirm hours directly before going.

cards.title: Study the Gothic Public Architecture
cards.subtitle: East Greene Street corridor
cards.notes: Follow East Greene Street to Statehouse Square and examine the Old Capitol’s granite steps, pointed arches, and towers.
cards.short_summary: A former statehouse whose exterior makes Georgia political history tangible.
cards.evidence_claim: Georgia’s Old Capitol Building is at 201 East Greene Street and features granite steps, pointed arches and large towers dating to its 1807 Gothic design.
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing may be possible from Statehouse Square; verify public interior access with Georgia Military College.

cards.title: Tour a Restored 1839 Residence
cards.subtitle: South Clarke Street corridor
cards.notes: Turn onto South Clarke Street and time your arrival for an hourly tour of the mansion’s restored 19th-century interior.
cards.short_summary: An interpreted house museum connecting architecture, politics and antebellum society.
cards.evidence_claim: The mansion at 120 South Clarke Street was completed in 1839, restored to its 1851 appearance and operates as a historic house museum.
cards.access_notes: Tours are listed Tuesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m., and Sunday, 2–4 p.m., beginning each hour; closures apply.

cards.title: Enter a Recreated Classroom
cards.subtitle: South Clarke Street corridor
cards.notes: Continue south on Clarke Street to explore the recreated classroom and learn how Davis supported students at Eddy High School.
cards.short_summary: A preserved educator’s home interpreting Black education and community care.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sallie Ellis Davis House at 301 South Clarke Street includes a recreated classroom and preserves the educator’s work with Eddy High School students.
cards.source_title: The Legacy of Sallie Ellis Davis: African American Educator in Milledgeville
cards.access_notes: Tours are offered Wednesdays and Fridays, selected weekends, and by arrangement; call 478-445-5889 to confirm.

cards.title: Locate the Eddy Tour’s Cemetery Stop
cards.subtitle: Liberty Street corridor at Franklin Street
cards.notes: Use the entrance map at Liberty and Franklin Streets to find documented burials, and keep your visit quiet and respectful.
cards.short_summary: A reflective Eddy Neighborhood stop tied to Black civic and military history.
cards.evidence_claim: Bone Cemetery is at Liberty and Franklin Streets and includes documented burials of physician B. J. Simmons and three Buffalo Soldiers from the 9th Cavalry.
cards.source_title: Exploring The Eddy Neighborhood: African American History in Milledgeville, Georgia
cards.access_notes: Use the cemetery map at the entrance, remain on established paths and observe respectful daylight visiting practices.
